title: Soil moisture interaction intervals crossed zero in four Cedar Creek samples in 2017-2022
abstract: We tested whether warming changed the drought soil-moisture contrast in released Cedar Creek records. We used two planting groups and two periods in 2017-2022. Complete panels contained 4-7 plots per test. The joint response minus the two separate responses was +0.004820, +0.008867, -0.000713 and -0.004289 cubic metres per cubic metre. All four corrected intervals included zero. Alternative panel and row weights gave the same broad result. The release does not establish repeated amplification or independent treatment action. Morning-only sampling, missing dates, no eligible 2018 visits, few plots and one site limit inference. The additive interpretation follows the paper and requires common control support. No biodiversity mechanism or pollution effect was tested. Code, source hashes, aggregate evidence and an external retrieval script support reproduction.

display.caption: Complete-plot additive soil-moisture interactions and four-test family intervals. All intervals cross zero. The early period has observations in 2017 and 2019 only.
